meta.note: Hyper-specific merchant/portal multipliers are not mapped into travel; see special_earn_rules.

inclusion_rules.grocery: Supermarkets and qualifying grocers; excludes wholesale clubs unless issuer explicitly codes them as grocery.
inclusion_rules.dining: Restaurants, cafes, bars, food delivery coded as dining.
inclusion_rules.transit: Public transit, parking, tolls, and commuting services that are not rideshare.
inclusion_rules.digital: Digital app/software/game/music purchases not billed as streaming subscriptions.
inclusion_rules.utilities: Home utilities and telecom billers when issuer separately rewards utility-type merchants.
inclusion_rules.bills: Pre-authorized recurring bill payments not otherwise mapped to utilities/streaming/digital.
inclusion_rules.travel: Non-portal travel spend (airlines, hotels, car rental, cruises, travel agencies) unless an issuer states portal-only acceleration.
inclusion_rules.other: Base earn for all uncategorized eligible purchases.

exclusion_rules: Merchant-, chain-, portal-, or redemption-dependent bonuses are stored in special_earn_rules and not promoted into base earn_rates.
Program-value assumptions (e.g., Aeroplan cents-per-point) do not change earn multipliers in earn_rates.
tie_break_rules: Use issuer merchant category coding (MCC) precedence when categories overlap.
If a transaction can map to rideshare or transit, rideshare wins only for app ride-hailing operators.
If a charge is both recurring and category-specific (e.g., streaming subscription), the specific category wins over bills.
If terms cite portal-only travel acceleration, keep baseline travel in travel and capture portal uplift in special_earn_rules.

meta.cards_sort_order: cards[] are sorted by issuer (asc), network (asc), card_name (asc), then id (asc); keep this order when adding/updating cards.
